description.narrative:
As violence by armed groups in Haiti’s capital continues to displace populations, many are seeking refuge in the southern region of the country. This has placed enormous pressure on host communities, which were already struggling to meet their basic needs. Torbeck is the third most affected commune in the South, hosting a large number of displaced people.
Among the most vulnerable groups are:
Women lacking sufficient financial means to care for themselves and their children. Elderly people who are entirely dependent on family support. Persons with disabilities, who are facing heightened suffering, even compared to non-disabled individuals who are already struggling. Displaced families, many of whom have been separated and spread among various host families. Some have built makeshift shelters on land left behind by deceased relatives. Women and girls in these households are particularly affected, often resorting to small-scale street vending (e.g. peanuts, mangoes, cosmetics) in public markets and city streets to earn a living.
The SCLR Project, to be implemented in Torbeck in 2025, seeks to address the following urgent needs:
Food Security: Many families lack sufficient quantity and quality of food. Access to Irrigation Water: Despite water availability, some farmland remains dry due to blocked irrigation channels. Adequate Shelter: Displaced individuals are living in inhumane conditions, with tarpaulin roofs exposed to the elements. Access to Healthcare: There is an urgent need for basic health services, including psychosocial support and chronic illness treatment. Access to Cash: Many displaced people, especially women, have no means to support their families or launch small businesses.
To support the most vulnerable crisis-affected communities, KORAL will provide micro-grants (ranging from USD 3,000 to 3,500) to at least seven (7) grassroots community-based organisations (CBOs).
Expected Results:
At least 175 families (approximately 875 vulnerable individuals) will directly benefit from the implementation of at least seven micro-projects led by CBOs, targeting their most urgent and immediate needs.
At least 14 CBO members (two per organisation) will have their capacities strengthened through training sessions on the following topics:
Micro-project design and development Financial management and reporting
